business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Dilutive Revenue-Based Financing for Digital Brands

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force since October 31, 2012
Panama-Canada Free Trade Agreement, in force since April 1, 2013
Panama-United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (1983), in force since 1985
Panama-Netherlands Bilateral Investment Treaty (2000), in force since 2002

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of Panama: Decree-Law No. 23 of December 30, 2015 (AML/CFT/CPF preventive framework, as amended and supplemented); Law No. 42 of 2000 (historical predecessor, repealed and replaced); Criminal Code (Law No. 14 of 2007), Articles 254-256 (money laundering offenses); Cabinet Decree No. 114 of 2017 (guidelines for non-financial subjects); Law No. 129 of 2020 (Beneficial Ownership Registry, implemented by DGI/MEF regulations and operational since 2021); binding AML circulars and resolutions of the Superintendencia de Bancos and the Intendencia de Sujetos No Financieros.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Full Power of Attorney (Poder) for incorporation and resident-agency representation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin, legalized by the competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs or designated authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy and recent proof of residential address of each director, officer, attorney-in-fact, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing authority in the country of origin (national identity or immigration department; utility or bank as issuer of address proof)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn Spanish translation where the registry requires

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Corporate Existence for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Register of Directors and Shareholders of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization followed by sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming active banking relationship and source-of-funds provenance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or direct bank confirmation; normally accepted without apostille at the resident agent's discretion, subject to direct verification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, attorneys-in-fact, and counterparty beneficiaries against: OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated terror and sanctions lists, and Panama's domestic PEP and AML/CFT alerts maintained by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); enhanced due diligence (EDD), including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, is applied to politically exposed persons, non-resident corporate shareholders in opaque jurisdictions, and royalty-intensive or digital-asset counterparty flows; screening is executed pre-onboarding and re-executed on any material change such as ownership transfer, capital increase, or new financing counterpart involvement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - online name-search and reservation service at https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa (certificate of name reservation issued via the registry's certified online or in-person desk)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The final corporate name must end with 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.'; the Registry operates entirely in Spanish and all filings, certifications, and registry annotations are rendered in Spanish; non-Spanish brand names are permissible when written in the Latin script and are transliterated into Spanish for the registry record; the proposed name must be distinguishable from all existing registrations and not phonetically identical in Spanish; any foreign-language document relied on during name clearance must be accompanied by a sworn Spanish translation (traducción jurada).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Bank / Banca / Financiera - requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá
Seguros / Reaseguro / Insurance - requires prior approval from the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros
Fondo de Inversión / Valores / Bolsa / Mercado de Valores - requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores
Fideicomiso / Trust / Fiduciaria - requires verified banking-fiduciary licensing status
Panamá / República de Panamá / Nacional / Oficial / Gobierno - protected official tokens requiring flag authorization
Cooperativa - requires authorization from the cooperative-sector regulator
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be corrected by filing a new reservation request online; upon formal rejection, the applicant may submit a petition to the Director General of the Registro Público within 5 business days stating the legal and factual grounds distinguishing the proposed name from the cited registry entry, and may file the hierarchical appeal (recurso de alzada) if the first petition is denied; while the appeal is pending, the applicant should reserve a defensible alternative name to protect the incorporation timeline; judicial recourse lies before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Suprema Corte de Justicia only after exhaustion of administrative remedies; reservation extensions are granted in successive 30-day periods upon payment of the registry tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not permissible as the statutory address: every Panamanian Sociedad Anónima must maintain a registered office at the physical office of a licensed resident agent (law firm, trust company, or corporate agent) in Panama, where corporate records, share registers, and UBO documentation are kept; the underlying commercial functions (royalty financing underwriting and fund administration) may be managed from a foreign back office, but the S.A.'s legal seat and the resident agent's physical address remain quotable and enforceable in all contracts and registry filings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate - approximately 15-20% annual likelihood of unannounced on-site inspection by the Intendencia de Sujetos No Financieros or the Unidad de Análisis Financiero; the probability rises to about 25-30% for enhanced-risk revenue-based financing vehicles without an established physical operational footprint or where nominee directors or shareholders are identified; inspections focus on the resident agent's premises and the S.A.'s statutory books, share ledger, and beneficial ownership file.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation certificate (búsqueda y reserva de nombre)
Notarization of Articles of Incorporation (escritura pública) before a Panamanian notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public of the First Judicial Circuit of Panama

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Inscription of the S.A. in the Registro Público and issuance of certified certificate of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff computed on the authorized capital floor bracket

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year licensed resident agent (registered office) fees, including coordination of the annual entity tax filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian corporate agent or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 400-550 for standard S.A. packages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of UBO and corporate documents (4 documents at USD 80 each)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent legalization authorities of the origin countries (Ministry of Foreign Affairs or consulates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular and market legalization fee benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of apostilled documents (4 documents at USD 100 each)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per certified translation page or document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO record filing with the Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Beneficiario Final)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 de Panamá (Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas), as amended by Ley 25 de 2015 (capital and share rules), Ley 4 de 2019 (tax transparency) and Decreto-Ley 5 de 2015 (Public Registry modernization); key sections: Art. 4 (capital), Art. 5 (object), Art. 12 (directors), Art. 26–31 (registered office and resident agent), Art. 45 (territorial scope).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Mercantil (Dirección de Sociedades Anónimas, Inserciones y Certificados)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Pacto Social y Estatutos) presentada e inscrita ante el Registro Público de Panamá
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. A nominal authorized capital (standard US$10,000, fully subscribed but not necessarily paid) is declared in the by-laws; no escrow or bank deposit requirement applies. Share capital may be expressed in any freely convertible currency and may be paid in cash, assets, or services under Art. 4 of Ley 32 de 1927.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION – ROYALTY FINANCING FUND, S.A.: RESOLVED: (1) That the share capital set forth in the Deed of Incorporation is hereby validly issued, subscribed, and fully confirmed in favor of the founding subscriber; (2) That the registered office is fixed at Calle 50, Plaza Corporativa, Panama City, Panama, where the resident agent shall receive service of process; (3) That Ana Isabel Vergara is appointed President, Carlos Rivera is appointed Secretary-Treasurer; (4) That the officers may open bank accounts, execute direct-debit ACH and wire-transfer payment rail agreements, and file the RUC, municipal Aviso de Operación and UAF AML registration; and (5) That the President may countersign certified extracts of this Resolution for third parties. FURTHER RESOLVED: That the corporate seal is adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and drafting of Pacto Social y Estatutos
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Certificados de Nombre, online portal rr.pp.gob.pa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed resident agent requests a name availability certificate and drafts the Escritura Pública containing the corporate object (ISIC 6499 royalty-based revenue financing), share classes, first directors, resident agent clause, and the registered office address.
required_dossiers: Name availability search request
Draft articles of incorporation
Power of attorney executed by the incorporator
Agente residente professional license copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, resubmit with two alternative denominations; no appeal fee is incurred, only a fresh administrative filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública of the Republic of Panama (licensed attorney acting as notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators and first directors execute the deed before a Panamanian notary; the notary verifies identities, attests signatures, seals the Escritura, and returns the first testimonio for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Draft deed in Spanish
Valid passports or Panamanian identity cards of incorporators and directors
Payment of notarial stamps and the official registration fee (approximately USD 300)
Name certificate issued by the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies inconsistent signatures or missing heirs' consents in succession scenarios, the parties re-appear to rectify the deed before the same notary; foreign documents must be apostilled and translated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Mercantil (Ventanilla de Inscripción / Título electrónico)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first testimonio of the notarized deed at the Mercantile Section or through the digital registry platform; pay the tariff stamp and inscription fee; obtain the Folio Electrónico de Persona Jurídica and the Certificado de Inscripción proving legal existence.
required_dossiers: First testimonio (notarial certified copy) of the Escritura Pública
Official registry fee payment receipt (USD-based tariff)
Form of formal request signed by the resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a Nota de Observación (e.g., defective corporate object or capital clause), the resident agent files a written subsanación or amends the deed by aclaratoria; inscription remains suspended until compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RUC obtainment and territorial tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Registro Único de Contribuyentes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the DGI digital platform (or attend the customer service office), file Form RUC-01, and attach the registered deed; obtain the RUC (also NIT) and configure territorial tax status, calling last quarter 18% rate only for Panama-source income (none for foreign royalty funding returns).
required_dossiers: Certificado de Inscripción from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the first board resolution appointing officers
Passport/national ID of directors and the resident agent
Lease agreement or letter of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RUC application is rejected due to address proof discrepancies, update the DGI electronic file with a corrected utility bill and the notarized registered office confirmation; if rejection persists, escalate administratively under DGI procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá – Dirección de Avisos de Operación via Sistema Único de Trámites del Usuario (SUNT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación on the SUNT portal for a 'servicios financieros – financiamiento basado en ingresos' office; pay the annual municipal fee (approximately USD 300–600 depending on annual gross expected revenue); the license certifies the physical address for lawful commercial operation.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Registry certificate of the S.A.
Lease agreement with proof of occupancy
Cuerpo de Bomberos inspection certificate (office use)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality returns the application for address or activity divergence, correct the code (ISIC 6499 equivalent in the municipal tariff) and resubmit digitally; no restart is required if amendments are filed within 8 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UAF registration as obligated subject (AML/CFT compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) – Sistema de Registro de Sujetos Obligados (FIDE/SIAF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the S.A. as an Obligated Subject under Ley 23 de 2015 via the UAF secure portal; append the compliance officer appointment resolution, submit the Medium_Risk_Enhanced risk matrix, and adopt internal AML policies covering direct-debit ACH and wire-transfer payment rails for the royalty financing fund.
required_dossiers: FIDE (Formulario Único de Identificación) for the legal entity
RUC and municipal Aviso de Operación
Board resolution appointing the Oficial de Cumplimiento
AML/CFT manual and transaction monitoring procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UAF requests corrections to the FIDE or risk matrix, the resident agent and compliance officer respond electronically within the stated deadline; failure to cure leads to a temporary suspension notice which is lifted upon compliance evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá and Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección de Comercio; no manufacturing or industrial permit is applicable as the entity operates a non-regulated financial vehicle with an administrative office only
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Municipal (financial services office) and UAF Subject Registration Certificate (Sujeto Obligado)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I – Exempt (administrative office activity; no full EIA or environmental registration applies)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission sources; municipal sanitary sewer compliance under MINSA norms. If the fund later installs a server or colocation pod on site, MiAMBIENTE low-impact activity registration is required with daytime noise limit (Lmax) of 60 dBA and proper e-waste handling under Ley 44 de 2021 (extended producer responsibility).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Inspección del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (fire safety per NFPA 101) mandatory for the leased office; structural load certificate from the Ministry of Public Works (MOP) or a licensed engineer confirming floor live load ≤ 245 kg/m2; occupational safety and health clearance by MITRADEL under Decreto Ejecutivo 83 de 2011, plus the employer registration at CSS (Seguro de Riesgos Profesionales) for workers' compensation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama; taxpayer portal: https://dgi.gob.pa (electronic services include e-Services, RUC registration, and tax return filing)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign legal entity must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) before engaging in taxable operations in Panama. The procedure is: (1) appoint a local resident agent or law firm; (2) file the RUC application with DGI using the company registry certificate, apostilled Articles of Incorporation, power of attorney, and identification of the legal representative; (3) register for the required fiscal obligations (income tax, ITBMS, and withholding) through the DGI portal or in-person at a DGI local office; (4) open a Panama bank account if payroll or local operations are anticipated; (5) if the entity imports or exports goods, obtain an importer/exporter code from the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MICI) and customs registration with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá (ANA). Issuance of the RUC typically takes 5–15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — Panama applies territorial source taxation. Non-resident-owned Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) is taxed at the entity level only on Panama-source income, while foreign-source income is generally exempt from Panamanian income tax. No pass-through eligibility exists under normal S.A. formation; the entity is the taxpayer. A Panama S.A. acting solely as an offshore royalty financing fund that receives foreign-source royalties or interest income (without Panamanian customers or operations) is taxed at 0% on that foreign income, provided the funds are not remitted into Panama's banking system in a manner creating Panama-source activity. The entity is, however, subject to the Annual Franchise Tax (B/.300) and possible DGI information declaration obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not offer a 'check-the-box' entity classification election comparable to the U.S. regime. The S.A. is per se a corporation taxable as a separate legal entity. Available elections include: (a) under the territorial regime, the taxpayer may elect to claim the 'Núcleo o Grupo Empresarial' (business group) regime for consolidated transfer pricing documentation; (b) a foreign company may elect to register as a 'Centro de Llamadas' or 'Sede Regional' under specific incentive laws if qualifying, but this is not relevant to a passive holding/financing fund; (c) for ITBMS, a taxpayer with annual gross income below the B/.36,000 threshold may elect the 'Pequeño Contribuyente' (small taxpayer) regime, which applies a simplified fixed monthly tax instead of full VAT accounting. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized under Panamanian domestic law; Panama is not an EU member and has no domestic hybrid-mismatch rule analogous to ATAD, though transfer pricing and general anti-abuse principles may apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panamanian Value Added Tax on Sales of Goods, Services, and Imports)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (PAB/USD) of annual gross taxable turnover from taxable activities as established in the Código Fiscal. Taxpayers whose annual gross revenue exceeds this threshold must register as regular ITBMS taxpayers. Below the threshold, a small taxpayer may register under the simplified 'Pequeño Contribuyente' regime paying a fixed monthly quota, unless the entity voluntarily registers for the regular regime. In all cases, any entity importing goods into Panama must register for ITBMS regardless of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing for all ITBMS registered taxpayers through the DGI's 'Facturación Electrónica' system, which is based on the Panamanian Facturación Electrónica (dgi.facturaelectronica.gob.pa) platform. Taxpayers must issue invoices using an authorized invoicing software or the DGI free web portal, with each invoice receiving a unique 'COD' (Código de Operación) generated by the DGI system after validation of the invoice data. Transmission and validation are done in near real-time using web services/API (REST/SOAP) or via the DGI online portal. Invoices must include a QR code containing the electronic invoice reference and the DGI validation code, and must be delivered electronically to the buyer. The mandate is phased; large taxpayers are fully subject to real-time interoperability, and all ITBMS taxpayers are required to use the system as of the DGI implementation calendar. There is no physical tax stamp for B2B invoices; digital validation is absolute for fiscal credit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% ITBMS) is available for (a) exports of tangible goods that physically leave Panama under a customs export declaration; (b) services exported to non-Panamanian recipients, including offshore services, when the benefit of the service is realized wholly outside Panama and the recipient is not a Panama resident; (c) goods and services supplied to qualifying 'Centro de Llamadas' or export processing zones (Zonas Francas) under relevant regimes; and (d) international maritime and air transport services. For the financing fund's royalty income, zero-rating applies only if the royalty or financing service is treated as an 'exported service' — the service recipient must be located abroad, the royalty payments must originate from outside Panama, and the fund must not have a Panamanian customer or fixed place of business where the services are deemed rendered. Panamanian source rules deem services rendered in Panama as taxed at the standard 7% rate, so the fund must document the foreign location of the payor and the foreign place of use or economic benefit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) accepted by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), evidencing physical departure of goods (for goods exports) or a service contract with a certificate of foreign client status
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (conocimiento de embarque) with exporter as shipper and non-Panamanian consignee

Inward Remittance Certificate (comprobante de remesa de divisas) issued by a Panamanian authorized bank or evidence of receipt of the export proceeds in a foreign bank account, plus the underlying invoices and contracts
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panamanian tax authorities, through DGI audits and anti-fraud programs, scrutinize export zero-rating claims by verifying the physical exit of goods, the genuineness of the foreign service recipient, and the actual receipt of convertible currency from abroad. A false or unjustified zero-rating claim triggers: (1) a clawback of the omitted ITBMS (the full 7% rate) plus price-level adjustments; (2) default interest computed from the original due date; (3) administrative fines of up to 200% of the evaded tax under Article 756 and related provisions of the Código Fiscal; (4) loss of supplier VAT input credits for the period; (5) criminal liability for tax fraud under Panama's criminal legislation (including Ley 70 de 2019 on tax crimes) for wilful falsification of export documentation, carrying custodial penalties and disqualification from obtaining export certifications. Additionally, customs penalties apply for false export declarations under the ANA regulations, and the taxpayer's RUC may be suspended, which blocks future exports and taxpayer status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No Central Bank or Foreign Exchange Administration exists. Banking supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) oversees fiscal policy and external-debt management. The U.S. dollar is legal tender, and the Panamanian balboa is a convertible nominal unit at par with no independent issuance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized, open-currency jurisdiction with no discernible distinction between current-account and capital-account convertibility. The balboa exists only as divisional coins physically interchangeable with U.S. coinage. There are no legal restrictions, licensing requirements, or periodic approval gates for profit remittance, dividend distribution, interest payments, royalty transfers, capital repatriation, or loan repayment to non-residents. The territorial tax system does not condition convertibility on tax clearance beyond standard withholding obligations on Panamanian-source income.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts. Exporters are free to maintain, disburse, or repatriate U.S. dollar proceeds in any form without obligation to sell foreign currency to any authority. Documentary export records and bank-related declarations remain the only compliance touchpoints, and these arise from trade finance and AML rules, not exchange-control regulations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low. Panama does not maintain a dedicated electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing framework under its Banking Law. Offshore digital EMIs can only reach the local market through a licensed Panamanian sponsor bank or through the SBP regulatory sandbox. A pure offshore EMI cannot independently hold a Panama S.A. account without local custody arrangements. Legal constraints include restrictions on accepting deposits from the public absent a banking license, the SBP's digital banking and sandbox oversight, and OFAC/AML screening obligations for all USD rails. Use of a licensed regional fintech as a settlement vehicle is permissible but not a replacement for a corporate banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandated for non-resident beneficial owners of medium-risk structures. The ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and at least one signatory with a Panamanian nexus must appear before the bank's compliance officer or a recognized correspondent bank for an in-person interview. Remote opening is rare and reserved for low-risk resident corporations. For a non-resident-owned Sociedad Anónima, banks ordinarily require a board resolution, notarized constitutional documents, UBO identification, and, where applicable, a power of attorney granted to a resident lawyer for ongoing administration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO chain involving a private interest foundation (PIF) or discretionary trust with nominee directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership waterfall from UBO to S.A.; authenticated foundation or trust deed; registry certificate of the foundation/trust; UBO passport and proof of residential address; written professional introduction from an AML-compliant law firm; notarized certification of source of funds for the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-based financing model lacks conventional invoicing and may be misclassified as unlicensed lending or securities activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Panamanian counsel confirming that the activity is non-regulated treasury/funding activity within ISIC 6499; fund offering memorandum or cash-flow model; fully executed revenue-financing agreements; royalty schedules and independent valuation note; Swiss/European banking references showing established trade finance history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent wire history or counterparty exposure to high-risk sanctions jurisdictions creating adverse media flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of audited bank statements; OFAC and UN sanctions screening clearances for all partners; transaction-by-transaction source-of-funds narrative; board declaration of no money-service business activity; evidence of economic substance in Panama or qualifying foreign jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legacy bearer-share indicia or issued bearer share certificate for an older Panamanian S.A.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registry-issued certificate of good standing; cancellation of bearer securities; sworn affidavit of continuing legal control; report of no bearer shares from the Registro Público; notarized board resolution adopting registered-share structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is routed by SWIFT MT103 for direct investment into the operational bank account, with SWIFT MT202 used for interbank cover. The wire must carry a clear purpose code consistent with the KYC file, usually 'Capital Contribution / Foreign Direct Investment' or 'Intercompany Loan' if debt is injected. The sending bank must reference the corporate registry number, the account holder's legal name, and a board resolution authorizing the injection. Panama banks require a source-of-funds certificate and an expressed tie to the financing fund's confirmed non-public, non-deposit business model. In practice, the first inbound wire is often held as capital escrow pending full UBO verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements clear via SWIFT MT103 to global beneficiaries, with trade settlement enhanced by documentary commercial letters of credit issued or confirmed by Panamanian banks against invoices, Bills of Lading, and temporary import documents. Domestic payments use ACH 'ABA' rails and real-time local clearing through the Panama Payment System; international royalty distributions are effected by SWIFT and correspond via the U.S. Federal Reserve / CHIPS network given full dollarization.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-currency forwards on EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and CHF/USD
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on currencies of Latin American revenue jurisdictions where deliverability is limited
Cross-currency basis swaps matching notional royalty and loan repayment schedules
FX option collars / zero-cost cylinders for EUR, GBP, and regional Latin peers
Plain vanilla USD interest-rate swaps tied to floating-rate debt portfolio exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de Sociedades) payment and accompanying corporate declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, paid via Caja General and recorded with Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 July each calendar year; corporations incorporated in the second half of the year pro-rate the first-year tax and must pay in the year of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus statutory interest; persistent non-payment can cause administrative suspension, refusal of registration acts, and after the applicable Registro Público procedure, strike-off of the corporation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation and UBO Declaration (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) acting with the Registro Público de Panamá through the Beneficial Owner Electronic Platform / resident agent custody system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the corporation's assigned confirmation window following the registration anniversary; any transfer of shares must be followed by an updated declaration within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance may result in administrative fines from USD 100 to USD 50,000, suspension of the entity's right to present registry filings, and possible dissolution if the resident agent resigns and is not replaced within the statutory period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Register Audit by the Resident Agent covering the Share Register, Directors Register, minute book, and UBO custody file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate registered office of the Sociedad Anónima; resident agent of record; no public filing required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed annually before the 31 July franchise tax deadline and upon any ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain and audit the statutory registers weakens evidentiary standing in Panamanian legal proceedings and may expose the resident agent and directors to regulatory liability; unresolved deficiencies can lead to loss of the resident agent and eventual administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required only for Panamanian legal entities that are publicly listed, regulated by a Panamanian supervisory authority, or that had gross revenue or taxable income in Panama exceeding USD 500,000 in the preceding fiscal year. This royalty financing fund, operated on a territorial-source basis with no Panamanian-source revenue, is not subject to a compulsory audit unless one of those thresholds is reached or a financing counterparty requires audited statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the Panamanian National Accounting Directorate; books may be maintained in United States dollars/Balboas, and tax accounting applies Panama's territorial-source income rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Panama Law 29 of 2015, as amended by Law 70 of 2019, the resident agent must obtain, verify, and maintain the beneficial ownership record. The corporation must confirm the UBO schedule annually within its assigned calendar window; any share transfer triggers an immediate updated declaration within 30 days. Failure to make the annual confirmation blocks corporate registry operations and can lead to fines and eventual strike-off.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholders' and board meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750–USD 1,500 per year, including resident agent, registered office, UBO declaration support, register maintenance, and annual compliance coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required below the statutory audit threshold; if an audit is triggered by local revenue or financing counterparty requirements, typical certified audit fees range from USD 3,500 to USD 8,000

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (5% for profits subject to Panama ISR)
